title: Weather and zero-shot forecasting models: backtest results for GB electricity demand (part 1 of 2)
claim: In a preregistered 960-day day-ahead backtest of GB national demand, giving every model the same honestly timed ECMWF forecasts cut error by 34% for a weekly-lag regression, 32% for Chronos-2 and 23% for Timestral-209M but not for TimesFM 2.5, and most of the models' edge over the regression disappeared.
why_relevant: Same design as our benchmark (zero-shot foundation models against a lag regression with identical forecast weather), on national demand a day ahead rather than PJM zones a week ahead.

title: PJM Cold-Spell Calibration Benchmark: When Cold-Spell Calibration Fails to Transfer
claim: Across four PJM extreme-cold events, 90% load-forecast intervals from three forecaster families lose coverage inside the events, and no conformal calibrator chosen without the target event restores it under a protocol frozen in advance.
why_relevant: Pre-registered probabilistic load benchmark on PJM itself with temperature-driven events, at day-ahead rather than week-ahead and about calibration rather than point error.

title: Benchmarking Time Series Foundation Models for Load Forecasting Under Covariate Uncertainty
claim: On three load datasets Chronos-2 is the most accurate of eight models, zero-shot and fine-tuned, when future covariates are known or well forecast, but it degrades as covariate forecasts get noisier, where TimesNet holds up better.
why_relevant: Tests exactly the oracle-versus-forecast weather distinction our two regimes separate, on electric load with a model we run (Chronos-2), at short-term horizons.

title: Assessing Covariate-Informed Grid Load Forecasting with a Time-Series Foundation Model
claim: On ISO New England and ENTSO-E load with weather and calendar covariates, fine-tuned Chronos-2 beats task-specific deep models at short horizons, while zero-shot Chronos-2 is less accurate than those models and its error grows faster with lead time.
why_relevant: Chronos-2 with temperature covariates on zonal ISO load, including how the error behaves as the horizon lengthens, which is the model in our primary comparison.

title: Zero-shot forecasting models and GB electricity demand: a preregistered test
claim: Without weather inputs, zero-shot Chronos-2 and Timestral-209M beat a weekly-lag regression on day-ahead GB demand by roughly 7 to 9 percent over 2024-01 to 2026-10, short of the 10 percent gain set in advance, and TimesFM 2.5 was no better than the regression.
why_relevant: The study our backtest design mirrors: pretrained models against a lag regression on national load with a preregistered 10 percent bar, univariate and day-ahead.
query: TimesFM OR Chronos-2 OR Timestral OR TabPFN-TS electricity load

title: EnergyBench: a live, gate-aligned benchmark of day-ahead forecasts for European power markets
claim: Over the first 32 live days, the same frozen weather covariates cut the error of each of ten foundation models by 37-51% in matched races, zero-shot models matched or beat a LightGBM trained on those covariates, and on load the best models were within 4-6% of the grid operators' forecasts.
why_relevant: Live test of foundation models with and without identical forecast-weather inputs on load among other series; day-ahead and European zones rather than week-ahead PJM.
query: electricity load forecasting foundation model benchmark

title: Lead-Time-Conditioned Convex Stacked Ensemble for Medium-Term Electricity Load Forecasting
claim: A stacked ensemble of nine models with separate convex weights for each of the seven lead days, fitted out of fold to avoid leakage, is proposed for weekly-ahead daily load forecasting and compared against its base models and a 7-day persistence baseline.
why_relevant: The only hit whose horizon is exactly one week ahead for electricity load; daily rather than hourly resolution.
query: week-ahead OR medium-term electricity load forecasting

title: Timestral: Mistral's family of time series foundation models (5M to 209M)
claim: Mistral released four zero-shot probabilistic forecasting models with past-only and known-future covariate support that run on CPUs, and reports the 209M model first among zero-shot models on GIFT-Eval, TIME and fev-bench.
why_relevant: A covariate-capable model already in runnable_models (ff_native_exog), released inside our scored window.

title: Combining Weather Forecast Aggregation and State-Space Models for Adaptive Probabilistic Electricity Load Forecasting
claim: Feeding an adaptive state-space GAM with forecasts from several weather providers, rather than one, improves both point and probabilistic forecasts of French national load, most clearly in the extreme quantiles.
why_relevant: Electric load with forecast weather as the known-future input and an explicit treatment of weather-forecast error, with a regression-family model close to our baseline.

title: TimesFM 3.0: natively multivariate zero-shot forecasting with covariates
claim: Google released TimesFM 3.0, a 330M-parameter model that forecasts several targets jointly with past-only and known-future covariates in one pass, and reports the best average rank among pretrained models on GIFT-Eval, fev-bench and TIME; the weights carry a non-commercial licence.
why_relevant: A model that takes temperature as a known-future covariate and is listed as ff_native_exog; its weights date falls inside our scored window.

title: Short-term load forecasting under EU-AI Act Requirements in Safety-Critical Environments: Results from a 41-day live challenge on the aggregated German transmission-grid load
claim: In a 41-day live day-ahead challenge on aggregated German load, a deterministic local pipeline with weather and calendar covariates beat the ENTSO-E day-ahead forecast and was competitive with large pretrained models such as Chronos-2.
why_relevant: Live hourly system-load forecasts with weather covariates, comparing a simple auditable model with Chronos-2, the same contrast as our primary comparison.
query: electricity load forecasting foundation model benchmark

title: t0: A Time-Series Foundation Model for Forecasting with Context
claim: The open-weight t0 models condition on known-future covariates, which raise skill by about six points across 30 tasks, rank third on GIFT-Eval and fev-bench, and cut the error of a lagged-price baseline by 38 percent on 29 months of hourly ERCOT prices.
why_relevant: Pretrained model with known-future covariates and reported results on hourly electricity demand and prices; listed in spec.yaml as runnable with temperature.

title: Physics-Informed Fractional Load Forecasting With Memory-Aware Break Detection for Reserve Scheduling
claim: A day-ahead load model with a fractional temperature kernel for building thermal inertia and joint estimation of breaks and long memory improves on the best of ten benchmarks by 15.7% and 10.3% MAPE on New England and Mid-Atlantic data.
why_relevant: A temperature-driven regression-style load model tested on Mid-Atlantic load, the region of our PJM zones; day-ahead rather than week-ahead.

title: Zero-shot foundation models on Belgian day-ahead electricity load
claim: Over the 365 days of 2025, zero-shot Chronos-2 and Timestral with calendar and previous-day temperature forecasts reach a day-ahead error on Belgian load about level with the grid operator's own forecast, within the confidence intervals.
why_relevant: Chronos-2 and Timestral with forecast (not observed) temperature on national load over a full year, at day-ahead rather than week-ahead.
query: TimesFM OR Chronos-2 OR Timestral OR TabPFN-TS electricity load

title: How Far Does Zero-Shot Go? A Leakage-Aware Evaluation of TimesFM 3 on Post-Release, Multivariate and Controlled Data
claim: Under a protocol frozen before the test data existed, TimesFM 3 beats a classical ensemble by about 16 percent in MASE on structured post-release data including electricity load, leads Chronos-2 by about 5 percent, and its 80 percent intervals cover only about 70 percent.
why_relevant: Leakage-aware test of a runnable pretrained model on data after its release, including electricity load, which matches our weeks-after-weights concern.

title: Zero-shot time-series foundation models against the Khepri v1.5 baselines for 96-hour carbon-intensity forecasts in nine Nordic bidding zones: a preregistered comparison
claim: In a preregistered comparison, zero-shot Timestral and Chronos-2 without covariates had about one percentage point lower MAPE than SARIMA and gradient-boosting baselines for 96-hour hourly carbon-intensity forecasts in nine Nordic zones in 2025, while a 14-origin post-release holdout was too small to decide.
why_relevant: Preregistered zonal, hourly, multi-day energy backtest of two models we run, with a post-weights holdout; the target is carbon intensity, not load, and no weather is used.

title: TimeH2O v1 (H2O.ai)
claim: H2O.ai published open weights for a pretrained forecasting model, TimeH2O v1; the model card was not read, so no accuracy claim is recorded here.
why_relevant: spec.yaml lists TimeH2O as runnable with temperature through FoundationForecast, so it could be measured on our benchmark; weights fall inside the scored window.

title: Replication package for "Battery charging, demand statistics and the evaluation of U.S. day-ahead load forecasts"
claim: An audit of Form EIA-930 data for 49 US balancing authorities finds that battery charging counted in published load accounts for much of the apparent rise in CAISO day-ahead forecast error, and re-scores benchmark comparisons accordingly.
why_relevant: About the quality of the EIA-930 demand series we score against and how its definition changes forecast evaluation; it is an audit, not a forecasting method.

title: Parameter-Efficient Adaptation of Time Series Foundation Models for Electrical Load Forecasting
claim: Across four load aggregation levels, pretrained MOIRAI and Chronos-2 beat seasonal naive and XGBoost baselines, rank-16 LoRA cuts MOIRAI's NMAE by 7.5% on average, and Chronos-2 starts more accurate and gains less from adaptation.
why_relevant: Chronos-2 zero-shot and adapted on electrical load from country to building level, against a tree baseline.
query: electricity load forecasting foundation model benchmark

title: Peak-Aware Short-Term Load Forecasting Across Distribution Grid Aggregation Levels
claim: On UK and Swiss open data at three aggregation levels, Chronos-2 has the lowest error in high-demand periods at every level, 20-51% below gradient-boosted models, and stays best or near best overall.
why_relevant: Chronos-2 against LightGBM on load, with a focus on peaks; distribution-level series and short horizons.
query: electricity load forecasting foundation model benchmark

title: Machine Learning and Time-Series Foundation Models for Day-Ahead Electricity Forecasting in a University Building
claim: On 57 test days for one university building, TimesFM 3.0 with covariates has the lowest day-ahead error, about 43 percent below a weekly seasonal naive, with XGBoost statistically close and covariates helping mainly on holidays.
why_relevant: A runnable pretrained model with weather covariates on hourly electricity use, but one building, observed weather and a 57-day test under our 90-day minimum.

title: Systematic Evaluation of TabPFN-TS and Chronos-2 for Zero-Shot Heat Load Forecasting in District Heating Networks
claim: With ambient temperature as a covariate, zero-shot Chronos-2 and TabPFN-TS beat all trained baselines on hourly 24-hour heat-load forecasts over a full year in two German networks, Chronos-2 slightly ahead.
why_relevant: Zero-shot models with temperature on an hourly energy load, with a perfect-weather main run and a forecast-weather sensitivity that parallel our two regimes; heat rather than electric load, day-ahead.

title: Choosing Load Forecasting Methods by Horizon, History and Hour: Reserve and Imbalance Evidence from Four Grids (companion data, protocol and code)
claim: A pre-specified protocol compares load forecasting methods on four grids at horizons from 1 to 180 days plus hourly day-ahead, with online selection by horizon and hour judged by reserve and imbalance measures.
why_relevant: Load forecasting across horizons that include a week, under a pre-specified protocol with a deviation log; the record gives the design, not the headline numbers.
query: electricity load forecasting foundation model benchmark

title: Multi-horizon forecasting of national electricity demand in Türkiye: run records, forecasts and trained models
claim: The record archives 759 training runs, sealed test forecasts and bootstrap draws for a multi-horizon study of Turkish national demand using calendar, holiday and temperature information; it states no headline result.
why_relevant: National electricity demand at several horizons with temperature inputs and sealed test forecasts; the result itself is not in the record.

title: On the Encoding of Calendar Features in Covariate-Informed Time Series Foundation Models
claim: Across four foundation models and nine datasets, the way calendar covariates are encoded changes zero-shot MASE by up to 9.9% on ordinary days and 83% on holidays within one model.
why_relevant: Shows that a fixed covariate encoding can change the ranking of covariate-aware models, which matters for how we pass inputs to every model.

title: The Hidden Look-Ahead: Point-in-Time Leakage in Electricity Market Data
claim: For ten weather-model configurations matched to GB auction gates over 2022 to 2026, choosing the latest forecast run issued before the gate picks a run not yet published on most delivery days for six of them, with an accuracy effect that varies in sign and size.
why_relevant: A check on the no-lookahead rule for our forecast-weather regime (lead-matched archived forecasts); it audits inputs and does not forecast load.

title: The Impact of Covariates on Zero-Shot Building Energy Forecasting
claim: With Chronos-2 on building consumption, day-type indicators as past and future covariates cut CV-RMSE from 14.58% to 10.41%, while weather covariates, forecast or observed, add little.
why_relevant: Measures what weather covariates add to zero-shot Chronos-2 on electricity consumption, with forecast and observed weather kept apart.

title: Forecasting Daily Household Electricity Demand in a Hot-Arid City: A Comparative Benchmark of Local, Global, Deep and Foundation Models on ESHED-38
claim: Over 48 weekly origins on 38 homes, zero-shot Chronos-2 is the most accurate model one day ahead and ties with TimesFM-2.5, Chronos-Bolt and an ensemble at one week, while recorded weather improved no model and appears to be unreliable.
why_relevant: Weekly-origin evaluation of zero-shot models at leads up to and beyond a week; household daily demand rather than hourly zonal load.
query: electricity load forecasting foundation model benchmark

title: Timer-M1: A Multivariate Time Series Foundation Model via Learning Primitives
claim: Timer-M1, a pretrained multivariate model trained with explicit target, past-only and known-future covariate roles, is reported first on the FEV and TIME benchmarks and second on GIFT-Eval.
why_relevant: A pretrained model designed for known-future covariates; no load result and not among the models we can run today.

title: Tabby: An Open Pretraining Recipe for Time Series Foundation Models
claim: Tabby, a 145M-parameter long-context probabilistic forecaster released with its full training recipe, is reported as competitive zero-shot on GIFT-Eval and the out-of-distribution TIME benchmark.
why_relevant: A pretrained model spec.yaml lists as runnable on load history only through FoundationForecast; univariate, with no load result.

title: Covariate Copies Count as Evidence in Time-Series Foundation Models
claim: On synthetic worlds with a Bayes reference, the study measures how covariate-aware foundation models weigh redundant covariates such as the same temperature supplied twice or from nearby stations.
why_relevant: Bears on how temperature should be passed to covariate-aware models (one series or several stations).

title: Forecasting Associations, Not Interventions: A Preregistered Causal Audit of Covariate-Aware Time Series Foundation Models
claim: On a preregistered grid with exact counterfactuals, Chronos-2, TiRex-2, TabPFN-TS and TimesFM-2.5 answer what-if covariate queries with the observational association rather than the interventional effect, and respond more confounded than a regression.
why_relevant: Preregistered test of how covariate-aware models use a known-future covariate; synthetic and physical systems, not load.

title: IBM Granite Time Series PatchTST-FM-r2
claim: IBM released a roughly 385M-parameter zero-shot probabilistic forecaster under Apache-2.0 and reports it second among replicable zero-shot models on GIFT-Eval and first among permissively licensed ones.
why_relevant: A permissively licensed pretrained model spec.yaml lists as runnable on load history only (PatchTSTFM); the announcement does not state covariate support.

title: Chronos-2 LoRA adapter for European hourly load
claim: A LoRA adapter for Chronos-2 tuned on 2015 to 2017 hourly load from five European countries reports a mean MASE of 0.387 against 0.402 for zero-shot Chronos-2 on 2019 day-ahead forecasts.
why_relevant: A load-specific variant of the model in our primary comparison; day-ahead, European, and the card does not say whether covariates are used.

title: Medium-Term Multi-Resolution Electric Load Forecasting using Economic Data and Foundation Model
claim: For French load forecast 1 to 48 months ahead at daily and monthly resolution, adding selected economic covariates to a tabular foundation model improves skill by about 20 percent over 2015 to 2025.
why_relevant: Electric load with weather and other covariates in a pretrained tabular model, but at horizons of months to years, far beyond a week.

title: Online Conditional Vine Copulas: Forecasting Electricity Demand
claim: An online, covariate-conditioned vine copula for joint distributional forecasts of net-demand in five GB regions outperforms unconditional Gaussian and vine copula benchmarks.
why_relevant: Regional electricity demand with covariates; probabilistic and multivariate rather than a week-ahead point forecast.

title: Foundation or Formula? A Simulation-Based Comparison of Google's TimesFM-3 and Classical Time-Series Models
claim: On 7200 simulated series under a pre-registered protocol, neither TimesFM-3 nor classical methods dominates: TimesFM-3 is never more than about 1.3 times worse than the best method at a 12-step horizon, but automatic ARIMA is over 20 percent better on long seasonal ARIMA data.
why_relevant: Pre-registered test of a runnable pretrained model against classical baselines on data it cannot have seen; synthetic series, not load, and no covariates.

title: Hybrid deep learning models for medium-term electricity load forecasting
claim: A hybrid residual model reaches about 4% MAPE for hourly demand at horizons of 720 to 2160 hours on one dataset, using climatological averages in place of future weather.
why_relevant: Hourly load at horizons beyond a week with an explicit rule against using future weather; one dataset.
query: week-ahead OR medium-term electricity load forecasting

title: A Later Test Set Is Not a New Domain: Pretraining Familiarity Survives a Contamination-Free Hold-Out
claim: On data published after every model's release, pretrained forecasters win five of seven groups, and their advantage tracks how familiar the domain is from the pretraining corpus rather than seasonal strength or spectral entropy.
why_relevant: Speaks to our weights rule (weeks after weights): a post-release window may not remove domain familiarity; not about load.

title: A survey and benchmark for household electricity forecasting: From statistical to foundation models
claim: A benchmark of 30 models from statistical to foundation models on household load, PV and battery series, with public code.
why_relevant: Includes zero-shot foundation models on electricity load; household level, and no headline number in the search summary.
query: electricity load forecasting foundation model benchmark

title: Ranking reliability in building level day ahead load forecasting: analysis code
claim: Sixteen forecasters including pretrained foundation models are evaluated under a ten-origin and a 238-origin protocol to measure how window length and the number of compared models change the reliability of rankings.
why_relevant: Evidence on how many origins a load-forecast ranking needs, which bears on our 52-origin design.

title: Foundation models for electricity price forecasting and battery arbitrage: Can they replace market-specific forecasting models?
claim: Of nine zero-shot variants from five model families tested on German, Polish and Spanish day-ahead prices over 2021 to 2025, only the TabPFN models consistently beat two specialised price-forecasting benchmarks, and that did not carry over to battery-arbitrage profit.
why_relevant: Multi-year zero-shot test of pretrained models against specialised baselines on an hourly energy series; prices, not load, at day-ahead.
query: electricity load forecasting foundation model benchmark

title: ElecLoad: Adaptive Electricity Load Forecasting Guided by Multiple Events
claim: A context-aware agent that reads notices, weather alerts and event schedules and splits the forecast horizon by event effects is reported as the most accurate method in most scenarios on several load datasets.
why_relevant: Electric load forecasting with weather-related context, but through text events and an LLM agent rather than a temperature series, and unlikely to run on a CPU laptop.

title: OpenSTEF 4.0: modular short-term energy forecasting with a foundation-model forecaster and a backtesting framework
claim: OpenSTEF 4.0 adds a learned ensemble of forecasters, a foundation-model forecaster and a backtesting and evaluation package designed to keep model comparisons free of future-data leakage.
why_relevant: An open load-forecasting library used by grid operators that now ships a foundation-model forecaster and a backtest harness.

title: Adaptive Residual Modeling for Scenario Learning in Probabilistic Load Forecasting
claim: A two-stage scenario model for feeder active and reactive power with a separate tail-calibration step cuts the 0.99-quantile pinball loss by roughly 30 to 85 percent against three baselines on one feeder dataset.
why_relevant: Probabilistic load forecasting with an environmental-response component, at feeder level and about extreme quantiles rather than zonal week-ahead error.

title: TabPFN-3.5: Technical Report
claim: Prior Labs' new tabular foundation model is reported to set the state of the art on tabular benchmarks and to bring stronger time-series forecasting through its task harness, without forecasting numbers in the abstract.
why_relevant: The base model behind TabPFN-TS, which takes known-future covariates and is in our runnable list as a univariate wrapper; the forecasting claim is unspecific.

title: From Shared Demand Patterns to Local Uncertainty: Probabilistic Load Forecasting by Mixing Compact Adaptations
claim: A shared forecaster with a small bank of low-dimensional adapters mixed per load improves point and probabilistic accuracy over statistical, neural and pretrained baselines on 590 synthetic-grid load profiles.
why_relevant: Load forecasting compared against pretrained baselines, at customer and transformer level on a synthetic dataset.

title: Probabilistic electrical power demand forecasting with uncertainty quantification
claim: Among four probabilistic methods compared on zonal power-consumption data, NGBoost gives the lowest errors and well-covered, fairly narrow intervals.
why_relevant: Zonal electricity consumption, but the abstract names no dataset, horizon or weather input, and no pretrained model.

title: SAP-RPT-TS: SAP's time series foundation model
claim: SAP announced a roughly 28M-parameter zero-shot forecasting model with past and future covariates and claims the lowest MASE and scaled quantile loss among the models it shows on fev-bench.
why_relevant: A covariate-aware model whose worked example is building energy with temperature as a future covariate; offered through SAP services with no open weights mentioned.

title: Zero-shot time series foundation models for statistical postprocessing of weather forecasts: analysis code
claim: The record holds the code of a study that uses TimesFM-3 and Chronos-2 zero-shot, with the ensemble mean as a covariate, to post-process 2 m temperature forecasts at German stations and compares them with statistical methods; the record itself gives no result.
why_relevant: Pretrained models with a known-future covariate on the temperature input our forecast regime depends on; the target is weather, not load.

title: SPECTRA: State-Space Exogenous Context and Temporal-Frequency Resolution Architecture for Probabilistic Energy Forecasting
claim: An architecture that separates deterministic and residual streams and aligns exogenous context with both achieves the best CRPS in 14 of 18 load, price, solar and wind settings, 5.74% below the strongest baselines on average.
why_relevant: Probabilistic load forecasting with exogenous inputs including temperature; a trained architecture, not a zero-shot model.

title: BQEB ForecastBench: Benchmarking AI Models for Smart Grid Forecasting Using BQEB-Data v1
claim: On an open smart-grid dataset with a chronological split, linear regression beats random forest and gradient boosting for both next-hour load and day-ahead price forecasting.
why_relevant: A reproducible load benchmark in which a plain regression wins, but at a one-hour horizon with no pretrained model.
query: electricity load forecasting foundation model benchmark

title: A controlled benchmark of temporal dependence for day-ahead electricity-demand discrepancies in Great Britain
claim: A retrospective benchmark over 364 days of 2024 compares independent, Gaussian-copula and empirical ensembles of GB day-ahead demand-forecast discrepancies on shared marginals and keeps its adverse and inconclusive findings.
why_relevant: About the time dependence of day-ahead demand forecast errors, which matters for scoring multi-hour windows; it does not forecast load itself.

title: Evaluating Accuracy and Probabilistic Reliability of Zero-Shot Time Series Foundation Models
claim: Six zero-shot foundation models beat statistical baselines and a supervised model on energy, traffic and financial data but trade point accuracy against calibration, with patch-based transformers miscalibrated at long horizons.
why_relevant: Zero-shot models on energy series across horizons; no covariates and no load-specific result in the abstract.
query: electricity load forecasting foundation model benchmark

title: Thaki EnergyLoad Forecaster v0.1
claim: Three LightGBM models for a single meter's load at 15-minute, 1-hour and 24-hour horizons, trained on a public 2011 to 2014 Portuguese dataset, report lower MASE than the best simple baseline on a six-month hold-out.
why_relevant: Electric load forecasting with a model family we already run, but per-meter, without weather inputs and at most a day ahead.

title: When Do Time Series Foundation Models Help Forecast Wind Energy Droughts? A Preregistered Evaluation (code and results)
claim: A preregistered study evaluates Chronos-2, TimesFM 2.5 and Moirai-2 with NWP covariates against climatology, model output statistics, quantile regression and a recurrent network for cumulative wind energy deficit in 16 regions.
why_relevant: Preregistered test of foundation models with forecast-weather covariates on an energy series; wind rather than load, and the record summary gives no result.
query: TimesFM OR Chronos-2 OR Timestral OR TabPFN-TS electricity load
